$comment: Source of truth for what this car exposes and how we know. Edit this, then run `pleiades registry` to regenerate docs/SIGNALS.md. A test asserts it agrees with Sources/Maia/ProprietarySignal.swift, so the two cannot drift.

provenance.measured: We proved it on this car. Requires a date, a method, and a log file.
provenance.standard: Defined by a public standard (SAE J1979, ISO 14229). True for any conforming car.
provenance.community: Third-party reverse engineering. Credible, not verified by us.
provenance.inferred: Reasoned from evidence but never directly tested. Treat as a hypothesis.
provenance.invented: Our own identifier, for bench signals with no known real counterpart.

confidence.confirmed: Measured, and discriminated from the alternatives that could have explained the same result.
confidence.candidate: A specific prediction we haven't tested. Says what would confirm or kill it.
confidence.unidentified: The identifier answers. We have no idea what it means. This is the work queue.
confidence.rejected: Investigated and ruled out. Recorded so nobody spends an evening on it twice.

sources.name: Measured on the car
sources.note: Enumerate a module, change one physical thing, enumerate again, diff. See docs/design/did-discovery.md.

sources.name: SAE J1979 / ISO 15031-5 standard OBD-II PIDs
sources.note: Hand-coded into Sources/Maia/PID.swift. Universal across post-1996 vehicles.

sources.name: ISO 14229 (UDS) standardised identifiers
sources.note: The F1xx block — VIN, part numbers, system name. Same on any UDS-compliant module.

sources.name: Wal33D/dtc-database
sources.note: 9,415 generic + 93 Subaru trouble codes, vendored to Sources/Maia/Resources/dtc-codes.json. mytrile/obd-trouble-codes was rejected for systematic row drift.

sources.name: commaai/opendbc — subaru_global
sources.note: Broadcast CAN frames on the main bus. Covers what openpilot needs, so plenty of engine internals are absent. Not reachable at the OBD port on this car.

sources.name: No public source exists
sources.note: Subaru publishes no mode-22 identifier table. Their dealer tool knows these internally. No community dataset covers them either.

buses.name: OBD-II diagnostic stub
buses.carries: Request/response diagnostics only — no broadcast traffic whatsoever
buses.evidence: 120 Ω across pins 6/14 (one terminator, so a stub) and zero broadcast frames observed on an error-free line

buses.name: main / powertrain CAN
buses.access: EyeSight camera connector, behind the rear-view mirror
buses.carries: Engine, chassis, and (per opendbc) BodyInfo + Dashlights
buses.note: Reachable with a comma 'Subaru C' harness as an inline passthrough, or by back-probing. Pinout: commaai/neo car_harness/v3/Subaru_C_Harness.pdf

buses.name: body CAN
buses.carries: Presumed home of the BIU, keyless, TPMS
buses.note: Whether the instrument cluster shares a bus with 0x75A is the open question that picks the route-3b install location. See docs/design/can-access.md.

modules.name: Integ. Unit
modules.role: Body integrated unit — doors, gate, lighting, chimes. Prime suspect for also being the CAN gateway.

signals.name: Rear gate
signals.method: Enumerated 0x75A three times: gate shut, gate open, passenger door open. 104E moved for the gate and ignored the door.
signals.note: The signal this whole project was started to get.

signals.name: Door front right
signals.method: Same three-state diff, inverted: tracked the passenger door and ignored the gate.

signals.name: Any opening
signals.method: Went true for both the gate and the passenger door — an aggregate, which is how it was told apart from the specific signals.

signals.name: Rear gate (page 11 mirror)
signals.method: Tracked the gate identically to 0x104E across all three states.
signals.note: Page 0x11 mirrors page 0x10. Kept as a cross-check; not polled.

signals.name: Door front left
signals.method: Neighbour of the two confirmed hits; sat at 00 through all three states. Never tested with this door open.
signals.note: Open the driver's door alone and re-enumerate to promote or kill it.

signals.name: Door rear left
signals.method: Neighbour of the confirmed hits; 00 throughout.

signals.name: Door rear right
signals.method: Neighbour of the confirmed hits; 00 throughout.

signals.name: (unknown — false positive)
signals.method: Moved A6 → A5 on the first diff and looked like a candidate. Across three runs the two-pass volatile filter caught it drifting on its own.

modules.name: Airbag System
modules.role: Restraints — seatbelt buckle switches. Spells booleans 01 unbuckled / 02 buckled, unlike 0x75A's 00/FF.

signals.name: Belt driver
signals.method: Four captures across belt states. 1046 went 01 to 02 when the driver belt was fastened and stayed there. Reads as the driver belt if the captures were cumulative; a single capture with only the passenger belt fastened settles it.

signals.name: Belt passenger
signals.method: Same four captures. 1047 moved one state later than 1046, when the passenger belt was fastened.

signals.name: (unknown — belt-shaped)
signals.method: Sits at 01 alongside the two confirmed buckles and never moved. Same shape, unknown seat.

modules.todo: Rear belts never appeared — page 23 is this module's distinctive page and was never swept, because the enumerator defaulted to a generic page list. Sweep it.

modules.name: Tire pressure monitor
modules.todo: Enumerate, then let pressure out of one tyre and re-enumerate to map corner to identifier.

modules.name: Keyless Access & Push Start (C)
modules.role: Keyless entry, driver side. Knows door and gate state for locking logic.

modules.name: 2.5 DOHC
modules.role: Engine control module. Answers the standard mode-01 PID set and holds the VIN at F190.
modules.note: Its 0x01xx page is 24 identifiers of mostly FF placeholders.

modules.name: Transmission
modules.role: TCM. Answers mode 01 but was never seen answering mode 22.

modules.name: EyeSight
modules.role: Driver assistance cameras. By far the richest module — 92 pages.

modules.name: VDC/Parking Brake System
modules.role: Stability control and electronic parking brake.

modules.name: (declined to answer F197)
modules.role: Unknown. The only module that would not give a name.
modules.todo: Try F187 (part number) or F18C (serial) to identify it. Page A0 is unique to this module.

broadcastFrames.name: BodyInfo
broadcastFrames.note: DOOR_OPEN_TRUNK is bit 36 — the broadcast counterpart of our measured 22 104E. Cross-checking the two is a free validation of both.

standardServices.name: Current data (PIDs)
standardServices.note: 57 supported on this car; 20 in Maia's catalog. Appendix A of architecture.md.

standardServices.name: ReadDataByIdentifier
standardServices.note: The service is standard; every identifier behind it on this car is manufacturer-private and unpublished.

openQuestions.question: Is the instrument cluster on the same bus as 0x75A?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Decides whether chime input interception is a mirror-shroud job or a dash teardown. Cutting at the gateway does nothing if the BIU and cluster share a bus, because that traffic never crosses it.
openQuestions.howToAnswer: Back-probe CAN H/L at the EyeSight connector and watch for cluster-sourced frames — odometer, warning state, unit preference.

openQuestions.question: Were the belt captures cumulative or isolated?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Decides whether 0x1046 is the driver belt or an aggregate. It is the only thing keeping the two belt signals at candidate instead of confirmed.
openQuestions.howToAnswer: One enumeration of 0x788 with ONLY the passenger belt fastened. If 0x1046 reads 01, it is the driver belt.

openQuestions.question: Where are the rear seatbelts?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Fastening the rear driver belt moved nothing on the pages swept.
openQuestions.howToAnswer: Sweep page 23 on 0x788 — its distinctive page, and never yet enumerated.

openQuestions.question: Is 0x75A also the CAN gateway?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: The module holding the gate bit would also be routing between networks — which changes what cutting near it does.
openQuestions.howToAnswer: If 0x75A transmits on the main bus while also holding body signals, it is on both networks.

openQuestions.question: What is module 0x78B?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: The only module that refused to answer F197. Unknown capability on the car.
openQuestions.howToAnswer: Try F187 (part number) or F18C (serial). Page A0 is unique to it and worth enumerating.

openQuestions.question: Which identifiers carry the seatbelt buckle switches?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Second-most-wanted chime after the gate, and currently invented rather than measured.
openQuestions.howToAnswer: Enumerate 0x788 belts-unbuckled, then buckled. Page 23 is its distinctive one.

openQuestions.question: Which identifiers carry per-wheel tyre pressure?
openQuestions.howToAnswer: Enumerate 0x75B, let pressure out of one tyre, re-enumerate. The corner that moves names itself.

openQuestions.question: Do the other three doors match the predicted neighbours?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: 0x104A/104C/104D are inferred, not measured — the registry currently claims three things it hasn't proven.
openQuestions.howToAnswer: Open one door at a time and re-enumerate 0x75A.

openQuestions.question: Are engine internals present on the main bus at all?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: opendbc decodes only what openpilot needs — coolant, fuel trims, oil temp are absent from its table. If the bus carries them undecoded, a tap replaces PID polling entirely; if not, mode 01 stays.
openQuestions.howToAnswer: Tap, capture, and look for frames that correlate with known PID values.

openQuestions.question: What are the other 186 identifiers on 0x75A?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: 191 answer, 5 are identified. The rest are the largest single pool of unknown vehicle state we have access to.
openQuestions.howToAnswer: Same mark/diff method, one physical change at a time. Lights, wipers, ignition position, gear selector, handbrake.

conventions.name: 22 xx00 is a support bitmask
conventions.detail: Four bytes, one bit per identifier, covering the 32 that follow, with the last bit chaining to the next block — the same convention mode-01 PID 00 uses. 0x74A answered 00 00 E0 50 at 0100, predicting 0111 0112 0113 011A 011C, which is exactly what it went on to answer.
conventions.consequence: 65,536 identifiers cost ~256 requests to map instead of 65,536.

conventions.name: An ELM327 in protocol 6 only receives 0x7E8–0x7EF
conventions.detail: The legislated OBD response window. Every body module is outside it and gets discarded in hardware. ATCF 700 + ATCM 700 widens it.
conventions.consequence: Without this a scan sees only the engine, and the car looks silent when it is answering.

conventions.name: This car answers FF for true, not 01
conventions.consequence: A decoder testing `== 1` reads every open tailgate as closed.

conventions.name: Boolean encoding is per-module, not per-car
conventions.detail: 0x75A answers latches 00 shut / FF open. 0x788 answers buckles 01 unbuckled / 02 buckled.
conventions.consequence: A 'non-zero means true' decoder reports every unfastened seatbelt as fastened. Encoding is declared per signal.
